Japan's 2027 Subaru WRX STI Sport R Brings the TY85 Heavy-Duty Manual Transmission Back
16 photos
Photo: Subaru / edited
Subaru has finally given Japanese car enthusiasts a regular-production manual for the VB-series WRX, and the TY85 is no regular manual. Boasting a solid mechanical rod linkage instead of a cable-operated setup for the TY75, the new tranny is paired with a familiar 2.4-liter turbo four-pot boxer and Symmetrical permanent all-wheel drive.
The STI Sport R for Japan should not be confused for a revival of the STI, though. There is no additional horsepower or torque, and the newcomer does not feature the Driver Controlled Center Differential of the VA-series WRX STI. Instead, a viscous-coupling center differential will have to suffice. The Japanese-market WRX lost its regular manual option when the previous-gen STI ended production.
Subaru rolled out the VB-generation S4 in 2021, but offered it exclusively with the continuously variable Subaru Performance Transmission. Between you and me, this box is anything but sporty. Enthusiasts got a small reprieve with the STI Sport#, a limited-run WRX for Japan that required a lottery to secure.
The response to the STI Sport+ was hardly subtle, with Subaru reporting more than 9,000 applications versus the 600-unit production run. Considering that the WRX STI Sport R with the TY85 targets monthly sales of 330 units in the automaker's home market, it should cross the 600-unit mark no later than January 2027.
Photo: Subaru Subaru ended TY85 production back in 2019 alongside the VA-series WRX STI. Being a heavy-duty box, said transmission uses a reinforced case, gears, and bearings, along with cast-iron shift forks, sliding ball bearings, double-cone synchros for 1st, 2nd, and reverse, plus a triple-cone synchronizer for 2nd. The shifter mechanism reduces shift play by a claimed 60 percent.
Better in terms of torque capacity over the TY75 as well, the TY85 is a clear upgrade. No upgrades can be found directly under the hood, though, for the FA24 engine produces the very same 271 horsepower as the CVT-powered S4 version of the WRX for Japan. However, it does generate a bit more peak torque.
Subaru claims 375 Newton-meters (277 pound-feet) from 2,000 through 4,800 revolutions per minute, and the Japanese automaker has also improved boost pressure response for a more rewarding driving experience. Subaru 's objective is linear and immediate torque delivery, and Subaru has also catered to the less talented among us by integrating automatic rev-matching technology.
Photo: Subaru Despite returning to the TY85, the STI Sport R does not feature the DCCD system we all know and love from the WRX STI. Its viscous coupler is joined by an open front diff and an open rear differential. In other words, side-to-side torque transfer is handled electronically through brake actuation. A front helical diff and a rear Torsen unit would have been so much cooler, but hey, it is what it is.
ZF is listed as the supplier of the STI Sport R's electronically controlled dampers, which feature dedicated tuning for winding roads, while Brembo manufactures the front six-piston brake calipers and rear two-piston units, along with all four drilled rotors. The monoblocks in question are joined by a Sport+ drive mode that is said to sharpen torque response.
Touring Assist, Lane Departure Prevention, and Emergency Lane Keep Assist are some of the standard EyeSight driver-assist suite's highlights. At launch, eight paint colors are on the menu, including WR Blue Pearl. Japanese customers have to spend 5,480,000 yen at the very least to get their hands on the STI Sport R, a figure that converts to 34,300 dollars at current exchange rates.

This Oversized Single-Level Tiny Home With Two Bedrooms Is Designed for Luxurious Everyday Living
15 photos
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes
Tiny living started as a shift toward minimalism and sustainability, but as tiny homes have grown in popularity, so have their size, features, and prices. Today’s tiny houses are no longer humble and basic. Instead of stripping life down to the bare essentials, many modern compact homes are true retreats packed with amenities, high-end appliances, and luxury finishes.
The Boho Park Model by Summit Tiny Homes is a great example of a high-end tiny house that offers comfort, style, and expensive commodities. At 42 feet (12.8 meters) long and 9.5 feet (2.9 meters) wide, it ranks among the Canadian builder’s largest models, offering a more spacious take on tiny living and a single-level layout designed to mimic the comfort and livability of a conventional dwelling.
Though many argue that oversized "tiny" homes often conflict with the main principles of sustainable living and the balance of needs versus wants, it’s always nice to know that downsizing your residence won’t come with compromises in terms of comfort.
Unlike traditional, basic tiny homes that tend to feel cramped and isolating, this larger model offers a more spacious, airy feel, and though it features two bedrooms on the main level, the central living room and kitchen areas are still generously sized, with plenty of room to move around. It’s a home that masterfully combines the benefits of small-space living with contemporary amenities, giving you space to do all your daily activities in comfort and even entertain guests.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Like all the tiny homes delivered by Summit Tiny Homes, this Boho PM unit displays excellent craftsmanship inside and out, beautiful finishes, and unique design details that make a big impact. On the outside, it showcases a modern look that pairs matte-black vertical board-and-batten siding with wood slat accents that add warmth and break up the dark cladding.
The house sits on a heavy-duty, quad-axle bumper-pull trailer fitted with leveling jacks at each corner and is finished with a standing-seam metal roof. Another aspect that highlights its contemporary style is the inclusion of not one but three floor-to-ceiling sliding glass doors that bring plenty of natural light into the interior and make the home feel more connected to its surroundings.
While the outside of the house might seem a little somber, the interior is nothing like it. The perfect way to describe it would be “grandiose beauty.” The color palette is bold, especially in the kitchen, the furniture pieces are expertly crafted, and the finishes are premium, contributing to a luxurious feel throughout. What’s more, the layout is fluid and natural light fills every corner, making this unit feel like a sanctuary on wheels.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes With a single-level configuration and two bedrooms on the main level, the Boho PM is specifically aimed at people who want to downsize their living space but don’t like compact dwellings with lofts because the idea of cramped spaces and hazardous ladders is not their cup of tea. The 400-square-foot (37-square-meter) footprint and extra-wide structure mean each functional area is commodious and functional.
The large central glass door opens directly into the kitchen area, which is not only very well appointed for a tiny house but also absolutely gorgeous. It features deep burgundy shaker-style cabinetry that extends to the ceiling and is accented by elongated brushed brass hardware. The beautiful cabinets are paired with white stone countertops and a tiled backsplash.
Though not very large, the kitchen fits full-size stainless steel appliances, including a gas range, an over-the-range microwave, and a refrigerator integrated inside a floor-to-ceiling cabinet. An apron-front farmhouse sink, fluted glass upper cabinets, and pull-out pantry sections are also included.
Boasting an L-shaped configuration, the cooking space also integrates a small peninsula with a flip-up counter extension that doubles as a breakfast bar separating the kitchen from the living area . Everything flows smoothly, and the lounge area, though a bit more minimalist, is equally stylish.
A white L-shaped sofa provides the perfect spot for relaxation, and a floating TV console is included on the opposite wall, ready to accommodate a large TV for entertainment.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Another highlight of this tiny house is the bedrooms. Located at either side of the house, they are both private thanks to discreet pocket doors that separate them from the open living areas. Inspired by Scandinavian design, they feature light wood floor-to-ceiling closets with fluted glass panels, low-profile beds, and under-cabinet LED strip lighting. They are also bathed in natural light and have direct access to the outside thanks to their own sliding glass doors.
The bed in the master bedroom is flanked by built-in wardrobes and the closet on the back wall also integrates a washer/dryer unit, adding even more functionality to the design. The other bedroom is designed with versatility in mind, fitted with a Murphy-style bed that integrates a fold-down desk underneath and an overhead shelving unit for books.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes No area inside this house will make you feel like you’re compromising. Even the compact walk-through bathroom is designed for indulgence. With a large glass-enclosed, fully tiled shower, a large burgundy vanity, an oval mirror, and a toilet, it looks just as stylish as the main living areas.
Spacious, stylish, and functional, the Boho park model is a spectacular home on wheels that proves Summit Tiny Homes has truly mastered the art of tiny home design. But all that comfort and premium aesthetic doesn’t come cheap. Pricing for this model starts from CAD$289,000, but custom features and personalized finishes will further increases the final cost. BMW Gives US EV Buyers $500 in Charging Credits and 25% IONNA Discount for One Year
8 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW of North America is offering both lessees and buyers of 2027 model year electric vehicles $500 in public charging credits. This offer presently covers the i5 and i7 sedans, along with the iX3 sport utility vehicle, combining a $300 BMW ChargingNetwork credit with another $200 reserved for IONNA stations. Buyers also receive a complimentary one-year IONNA membership.
This membership cuts charging costs by 25 percent. Both the complimentary membership and the charging credits expire after one year from the date of retail delivery or the lease commencement date. Customers can use the My BMW smartphone app to locate participating charging stations, initiate charging sessions, and track available credits.
IONNA participates in BMW ChargingNetwork, meaning that customers can use both credit balances at IONNA stations. The membership discount, therefore, can turn a $20 charging session into $15 after the 25 percent discount. In other words, the membership discount turns $500 into a little over $666 because the customer pays 75 percent of the normal charging price.
Applicable taxes and fees can understandably affect the final amount. As of this writing, the BMW ChargingNetwork provides access to more than 180,000 public charging points in the US market alone. The wider provider list includes ChargePoint, EVgo, Electrify America, Tesla Superchargers, and Shell Recharge. There is, however, a little catch here.
Per the IONNA network's FAQ page, 2027 model year BMW electric vehicle customers can't redeem their promotional credits at every one of those locations. IONNA excludes both Electrify America and the Tesla Supercharger network, though customers can still access both. In addition to IONNA, participating providers include ChargePoint, EVgo, and Shell Recharge.
Photo: BMW The 25 percent reduction advertised by the Bavarian company does not disappear when the $500 charging credits balance reaches zero. Customers will continue receiving this reduction for the remainder of the 12-month complimentary membership period, yet subsequent bills will be charged to the registered payment method.
After the 12-month period, IONNA applies a 10 percent charging discount. After enrolling through the My BMW app, customers have to open Charging, proceed to Services and Charging Wallet, select BMW ChargingNetwork, accept the relevant T&Cs, add a valid payment method, and set up the IONNA membership.
As noted earlier, the offer currently applies to the model year 2027 BMW i5, i7, and iX3. Going forward, BMW of North America will expand its battery-electric lineup in the first quarter of 2027 with the market launch of the i3 sedan and iX5 sport utility vehicle.
An exceptional machine that promises up to 468 miles (753 kilometers) of range at launch, the i3 needs 4.5 seconds to hit 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour). Charging is pretty quick as well, with BMW of North America claiming 21 minutes from 10 to 80 percent in the most optimal of conditions.
Gifted with a larger high-voltage battery, but also a lot heavier, the iX5 can't do better than 456 miles (734 kilometers) and 22 minutes, respectively. The only powertrain advertised on BMW's US website right now is a dual-motor affair with 570 horsepower to its name.

Normad Is a Cozy Camper Van That Adds a Splash of Purple to a Bright, Feature-Rich Interior
18 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / New Jersey Outdoor Adventures
A surprising number of people choose to travel by camper in the UK. Consequently, there are various companies that specialize in creating homes on wheels there. One of them is the simply and appropriately named "Vanlife Conversions." Today, I'm checking out one of its last project from last year.
Meet Normad, a camper built on a 6-meter-long Fiat Ducato. Its creator, Vanlife Conversions, is an Essex, UK-based company that turns vans into premium, off-grid-ready mobile homes.
Vanlife Conversions offers three layouts upon which you can base your conversions, which can of course be further personalized as needed: Milo, Rudi, and Kunu – this rig is built on the latter, which stands out with a fixed bed, generous garage, and versatile seating arrangements.
Before we take a closer look at those, let's see what we can find on the outside. Unlike some other camper vans we've covered here on autoevolution, this van doesn't have many upgrades. Despite that, it's still relatively obvious that it's a camper, at least to someone who's familiar with campers.
You'll notice that Vanlife Conversions added several windows on the sides and at the rear, as well as power and water hookups. What's more, the company upgraded the single leaf suspension on the back of the vehicle to a twin leaf suspension that can support the extra load coming from the conversion.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / New Jersey Outdoor Adventures The only other notable mods are on the roof: a Thule Omnistor awning, a Maxxair vent fan, and a 585 W solar array. Finally, you get a roll-down Van Essential mosquito net covering the entire entrance.
Stepping inside, you'll feel like you just entered a tiny apartment and not a van thanks to the homey, welcoming design. The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a large curtain to separate the two areas for more privacy and better insulation.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for a slatted ceiling with a white background, white laminated cabinetry, white walls, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by some purple accents, such as curtains, pillows, the cushion textile upholstery, and a subway tile backsplash – yes, they're all purple.
The passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, allowing you to turn it around to face the back of the van. You can also set up a swivel table by using a Lagun mount attached to the B-pillar.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / New Jersey Outdoor Adventures Straight ahead of the entrance, Vanlife Conversions devised a bathroom, hidden behind a tall standard door with an arched mirror and hooks for hanging stuff on the inside.
The bathroom boasts a Nature's Head composting toilet, a wall cubby for shampoos and soaps, a shower with a handheld wand, and an overhead storage cabinet. Moreover, the bathroom's design, with walls made up of large marble-imitating tiles, nicely matches the rest of the interior aesthetic.
Next, we have the kitchen on the driver's side. It features an oven with a three-burner stove, a butcher block oak countertop, a deep white sink with a cover, and a small fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
Two overhead cabinets, three drawers, a pull-out pantry, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / New Jersey Outdoor Adventures On the opposite side, you'll come across a simple but effective seating area. It comprises two benches with a Lagun table between them.
Here's where things become really flexible – the bench toward the front is attached to L-Tracks integrated into the floor, allowing you to easily adjust its position front to back as needed. Furthermore, you can use the tabletop to connect the two benches, rearrange the cushions, and create a small bed fit for a child or a pet.
The rear part of the living space is reserved for relaxing and sleeping, as it's taken up by a large bed with an east to west arrangement (meaning it's arranged from side to side).
It also offers a long overhead shelf, a vent fan, and the "command center" for the utilities, which includes a battery monitor, a smart switch panel, and a thermostat for a Truma Combi heater that provides both heated air and hot water.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / New Jersey Outdoor Adventures Finally, the area underneath the bedroom was transformed into a spacious garage. Besides offering room for storage in the middle, the garage accommodates the utility systems in boxes on the sides.
Power is on the left side. The customer opted for a simpler Victron electrical system in this rig – its highlights are a 160 Ah battery and a 600 W inverter.
On plumbing, the van is equipped with two under-mounted, insulated tanks, one for fresh water and the other for grey water. The vehicle's underside also holds a 25-liter LPG tank.
All in all, Vanlife Conversions created a home on wheels that not only looks fantastic but also packs all you need to hit the road without worrying about comfort.

Dongfeng Nissan officially opened the early order book on its new NX7 hybrid yesterday, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a $20,000 price tag.
When the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range. The company’s latest 2027 Rogue Hybrid is a step in the right direction , using a gas engine to generate electricity for a pair of electric drive motors that deliver a driving experience that’s remarkably similar to a “pure” electric car – but without a plug, it’s still entirely dependent on fossil fuels . The new Dongfeng Nissan NX7, though? That’s a different story.
The plug-in hybrid Dongfeng Nissan NX7 might be called a “long range hybrid” in the same sense that Volvo’s Euro-market XC70 is , in that it’s an EV for the 360-odd days a year that you’re driving less than 200 miles, and an ICE vehicle for the handful of days you drive more. And if you’re one of those people who thinks stopping on road trips is a character flaw, a fully charged and topped off NX7 will take you an astonishing 1,666 km (~1,035 miles) from where you started.
Covering all the angles
Dongfeng Nissan NX7.
The new NX7 could be an ideal lilypad vehicle for North American drivers who are either too afraid of being caught without a charger or too invested in the outcome of one or more dumb oil wars to confidently make the switch to EV – and, even at twice the 129,900 yuan ($~19,400) asking price, I think it would be a hit.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
For that money, NX7 buyers get an absolutely loaded Model Y-sized crossover (they’re within 1/4″ of each other in length), with a 17.3″ central touchscreen, a fully digital instrument cluster, and (on higher-spec models) a positively massive 55″ augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor and running on Nissan OS 3.0 with an AI-powered voice assistant developed with iFlytek that, Nissan claims, can recognize natural-language commands, remember user preferences, and even recognize occupants, adjusting vehicle settings accordingly.
On top-shelf models, the NX7 cabins get “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats that use sensors and air-cushion arrays to dynamically adjust for maximum comfort, and include heating, ventilation, and a 12-point SPA-level massage function. The front seats can be fully reclined to create a bed-like configuration that will be familiar to Cube owners. The NX7 even offers an on-board refrigerator and motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by as much as 83% (which, like, I wouldn’t want to be the one to test that – but seems cool).
Power comes from a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated internal combustion engine making 98 hp that’s paired to a 228 hp electric drive motor and the previously mentioned 40.9 kWh LFP battery. It’s not immediately clear if the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system like a Prius or a series-hybrid-plus-plug setup, but Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe a pretty versatile arrangement with four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation – which means the vehicle can theoretically use the ICE motor as a generator, drive the wheels mechanically, or work alongside the electric motor, depending on what the operating conditions call for. Whether any or all four modes make it to production on the NX7 remains to be seen, but it’s an intriguing bit of engineering for a vehicle promising nearly 200 miles of electric driving range.
The final production version will be shown to the public for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show later this month, but you can let us know what you think of the new NX7 in the comments, today.

AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 Chip Hero
Last week we witnessed the launch of AMD’s EPYC 9006 “Venice” series of server CPUs . AMD’s latest generation of server chips, the Venice launch marked an important inflection point on AMD’s server CPU business for a few different reasons. Not only was it the company’s first Zen 6 architecture chip family with all of the performance and feature benefits that entails, but it also marked a larger shift in AMD’s business. For the Zen 6 generation, at least, servers are now coming first for the company – and what was once one of the last products to launch with a new architecture is now the first.
That shift towards prioritizing servers was not just for AMD’s commercial operations, either. Alongside the company’s standard EPYC 9006, AMD went one step further and launched their EPYC Embedded 9006 chip family as well. The highly validated variant of AMD’s server chips that is meant for more foundational roles has never before launched at the same time as the traditional commercial chips, underscoring just how much things have changed for AMD in the past couple of years.
It also means that we have a whole other EPYC product stack to talk about, and one that is aimed at a somewhat different market segment to boot.
Though whether it is commercial EPYC or EPYC embedded, AMD’s technical strengths remain the same. The Venice SP7 platform brings with it significant increases in core counts, energy efficiency, I/O bandwidth, memory bandwidth, and more. And AMD expects that its embedded customers are just as much in need of the extra performance as the rank and file (and AI) customers who have been scooping up standard EPYC chips.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 Overview
These days, AMD’s complete EPYC embedded portfolio stretches from chips with a handful of cores all the way up to 256 cores, reaching parity with AMD’s best server chips. The higher-end chips have always been derived from AMD’s server and desktop platforms, and that has not changed for the EPYC Embedded 9006 series.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Embedded Lineup
In this case, the embedded version of the 9006 Venice family is adopting the SP7 platform wholesale. Which means it gets access to features such as 16 channel DDR5-8000/MRDRIMM-12800 support, 96 lanes of PCIe Gen6/CXL 3.1, the Zen 6/Zen 6c architectures, and AMD’s suite of security features for enterprise computing.
AMD EPYC Embedded: Generation on Generation
 | Embedded 9004 | Embedded 9005 | Embedded 9006
Codename | Genoa | Turin | Venice
Microarchitecture | Zen 4 | Zen 5c | Zen 6c
Core Manufacturing | 5nm | 3nm | 2nm
Max Cores/Threads | 128/256 | 192/384 | 256/512
Core Complex | 16 + 32MB | 16 + 32MB | 32 + 128MB
Memory Support | 12x DDR5-4800 | 12x DDR5-6400 | 16x DDR5-8000 / MRDIMM-12800
Memory Capacity | 6TB | 6TB | 8TB
PCIe (1P) | 5.0 x128 | 5.0 x128 | 6.0 x96
Socket | SP5 | SP5 | SP7
Peak Power | 400W | 500W | 600W
Where the EPYC Embedded 9006 lineup will chiefly differ from AMD’s commercial server operations is in regard to the chip availability and product support lifecycles. AMD will offer the 9006 embedded chips for at least 7 years, and they will be supporting the chips for longer.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Long Term Support
As well, the upgrade to the SP7 platform means that AMD’s embedded customers now get to reset the clock in terms of upgradability as compared to the SP5 platform. AMD will be reusing the SP7 platform for the next generation of chips (codenamed Florence), which means that designs being created today can be reused/upgraded in the future to use the newer chips without having to redesign or revalidate the entire platform.
All of which are important features for AMD’s target market of embedded users, who, even more than commercial server customers, move at a slower, more deliberate and conservative pace with their hardware designs and release cadences. The typical goal being to release a design for years, and support it for even longer.
Target Markets: ATE, Firewalls, and Enterprise Storage
Though the EPYC Embedded 9006 processors are being made available to AMD’s entire embedded customer base, the company has a few specific ideas in mind for what the best classes of products are for the new EPYC chips. Especially with the top-end of the new 9006 stack pushing total compute throughput harder than ever, these are the workloads that AMD (and its marketing arm) have been looking at.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Target Markets
Broadly speaking, AMD is chasing three particular markets with EPYC Embedded 9006: automatic test equipment (ATE) for semiconductor development, high-end firewalls, and enterprise storage controllers. All of which fall under the umbrella of long-lived infrastructure, and all of which are also tangential to the AI market in some form or another.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Firewalls
Firewalls are the most straightforward. With agentic AI systems pushing around more data than ever, faster firewalls are needed to keep up, be it by processing more data or being able to handle more complex (and thus CPU-intensive) policies. Even with the significant amount of offload acceleration in firewall appliances, they can still be quite CPU-intensive.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Enterprise Storage
Similarly, AI computing demand is driving up storage demand as well. With rackscale systems making heavy use of dedicated storage boxes, a fast CPU is needed to operate those storage systems – and AMD would like it to be theirs. Coupled with that, the 9006 family marks the introduction of PCIe Gen6 support on AMD’s EPYC Embedded platform, so for storage systems that are not using a PCIe switch of some kind, native PCIe Gen6 support is the key to getting the most out of the first generation of PCIe Gen6 SSDs.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Automatic Test Equipment
Finally, in a less conventional role, AMD is targeting the ATE market in this generation of EPYC Embedded. Automatic test equipment is not normally a very visible market, as the need for equipment is clustered around engineering firms rather than the hyperscalers, neoclouds, and other data centers that are deploying hardware in large volumes. But according to AMD, they are expecting a fresh jump in demand here due to all of the new technologies in play with this generation of hardware. Faster DDR5 RDIMMs, MRDIMMs, PCIe Gen6/CXL 3.1, and more. All of which will require new component designs and then significant validation of those designs.
More than anything else, this one seems to be AMD flexing at being among the first vendors to make a server processor with all of these features widely available. Intel is months away, and the various Arm-based operations are still ramping up their own hardware.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Memory and Bandwidth
Though for AMD Embedded customers who are making heavy use of PCIe connectivity, they will have to contend with a bit less of it overall. While the SP5 platform supported 128 lanes of PCIe Gen5, the SP7 platform only supports 96 lanes of PCIe Gen6 – so while the lanes are faster, there are fewer of them overall.
Final Words
Wrapping things up, with this month’s launch of their Venice server chips and their related EPYC product lines, we are seeing first-hand how AMD’s processor releases cadences have shifted significantly. With an emphasis on getting server processors out the door first, the lead products for a new CPU microarchitecture have become the EPYC family. And not just AMD’s standard commercial chips, but their EPYC Embedded chips as well, bringing the latter line from one of the last to launch to one of the first. It is a major change that goes to show just how important the EPYC Embedded lineup has become to AMD’s overall plans.
AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 – Summary
As for how AMD’s embedded customers will put the new chips and all of their new features to good use, the wait should not be very long, either. AMD is already making the 128 core EPYC Embedded 9756 available this month. The other 5 chips will quickly follow in late December.

Embedded 9966 | 192 | 384 | 4.1 GHz | 3.05 GHz | 768 MB | 600W
Embedded 9846 | 168 | 336 | 4.1 GHz | 2.9 GHz | 768 MB | 500W
Embedded 9756 | 128 | 256 | 4.1 GHz | 3.2 GHz | 512 MB | 500W

Keyvany Porroo Looks Like a Million-Dollar Ferrari Transformer in Dubai
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | keyvanyuae
Have you ever looked at the Ferrari Purosangue and thought that it does not look nowhere near as aggressive as it should be? Well, regardless of your answer, several tuners have, and they have launched all kinds of upgrades for the Prancing Horse’s first-ever high-riding vehicle.
Keyvany is one of them, and their Porroo take on this model is not exactly brand new. However, the project pictured above is, hence why we decided to share it with you. After all, when was the last time you’ve seen something like this against Dubai’s skyline? And we have to admit that it definitely fits the scenery, though in other parts of the world, this thing would be a lot more controversial. Notice how I didn’t say kitschy ? Oh, wait...
Anyway, kitschy or not, this build definitely turns heads wherever it goes, regardless of what language bystanders speak, and how much money they have in the bank. And plenty of them is a must if they dream about owning such a thing, because while the tuner hasn’t said anything about the finances in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, we are convinced that this thing is likely a seven-digit affair.
After all, the stock Ferrari Purosangue is already a very pricey cookie, kicking off at over $400,000 in the United States of America, and it costs close to $600,000 in Dubai (United Arab Emirates). And that’s before factoring in any boxes you may want to tick on the options list and the dealer fees. And obviously the aftermarket makeover, which tends to make these things ridiculously expensive. Thus, now you know why it is on the pricey side of things.
Photo: Instagram | keyvanyuae As for the things that make it more special, these include the numerous add-ons and replacements on the outside. The hood, for instance, is part of the latter category, as it now looks a heck of a lot more aggressive than the standard one. The flicks on the sides of the front bumper, the splitter, and other add-ons contribute to the special looks. It seems that there are also some wheel arch attachments, as well as some new trim at the sides.
And we are not done with the profile, because the side skirts are also new and quite massive. As if the ducktail spoiler wasn’t enough, this tuned Ferrari Purosangue also features a roof-mounted wing. And it also has new trim on the rear pillars, and an entirely new diffuser with blades on the sides and what seems to be an extra brake light mounted between the fins.
Keyvany’s logo bedecks certain elements on the outside. The car (it’s actually a crossover if you forgot) in question seems to ride closer to the ground, so a suspension upgrade is likely part of the aftermarket makeover. The wheels are also new, and they mix black and yellow, just like the rest of the exterior. The tinted lighting units seem to be the final touch on the outside.
This tuner is definitely no stranger to modifying cockpits, reupholstering them in leather and Alcantara, often in lively colors, and replacing the trim, seatbelts, and other elements with its own components. And chances are that the Ferrari Purosangue in question also has a custom interior. However, Keyvany hasn’t dropped any images of it at the time of writing, so you may want to take this information with the proverbial pinch of salt.
Photo: Instagram | keyvanyuae They also haven’t mentioned anything about this particular build in the Instagram post shared at the bottom of the story, other than the projects name, which is the Keyvany Porroo, as we already told you. Thus, we have no idea whether a power boost is part of the tuning job.
If it isn’t, then this Ferrari Purosangue should still have 715 hp (725 ps/533 kW) and 528 pound-feet (716 Nm) of torque to play with. The model is powered by an old-school naturally aspirated V12 engine with a 6.5-liter displacement, which can be revved all the way up to 8,250 rpm. The 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration takes just 3.3 seconds with no outside intervention. The model will reach 124 mph (200 kph) in 10.6 seconds after taking off, and the top speed is over mph (310 kph), the spec sheet shows.
Now, while Keyvany may not have had much to say about this project, it does encourage interested parties to reach out to them in order to commission theirs. And as we already told you, the pricing details are being kept a secret. But then again, this is one of those cases of if you have to ask how much it costs, you probably cannot afford it. That said, if money were the least of your worries, would you want to own a Keyvany Porroo version of the Ferrari Purosangue? 1965 Oldsmobile Cutlass Rescued After Decades in the Woods Gets Mangled at Demolition Derby
12 photos
Photo: Rust Wrangler/YouTube
Many classic cars are still rotting away in junkyards, barns, and various other places. And it's not uncommon to see them being rescued. Some make it back on the road, while others become parts cars. This 1965 Oldsmobile Cutlass , however, wasn't very lucky. Although it was saved from becoming a rust bucket, it was sent to its ultimate death at the demolition derby.
The second-gen Cutlass was found "deep in the woods of the Pacific Northwest," where it had been sitting for a very long time. And judging by the fact that it was buried deep in the ground and covered in vegetation, I'd estimate that "very long time" to at least three decades.
But while that's enough to render any classic into a piece of junk, our host, YouTube's "Rust Wrangler," managed to get it running and driving right there in the woods. That's mighty impressive for a mill that hasn't had a sip of gasoline in decades.
Speaking of which, this Cutlass was born with a 330-cubic-inch (5.4-liter) V8 engine. Called the Jetfire Rocket, this mill developed between 250 and 325 horsepower, depending on the carburetor and compression ratio. It slotted between the base 225-cubic-inch (3.7-liter) inline-six (155 horsepower) and the 400-cubic-inch (6.6-liter) V8. The latter came with 345 horsepower and was exclusive to the 442 package .
Once it was hauled back at the owner's shop. the Cutlass got its first proper cleaning in decades. And surprisingly enough, the car was pretty clean in terms of rust, and it still had some of its original paint intact.
This type of condition is often enough to persuade enthusiasts to fix the car and put it back on the road, but our host had different plans for this Olds all along. The Cutlass was stripped off of all unnecessary components, got some metal plates to seal the doors shut, got a quick paint job, and was enlisted in a demolition derby. It happened only one week after it was rescued from the woods.
Needless to say, the Olds didn't stand a chance in the pit and had to be dragged away by a tractor, with both its front and rear ends heavily smashed. The brave V8 engine that agreed to spring back to life in the woods gave its final breath in a big cloud of smoke.
Mangled and with a cracked frame, the Cutlass is no longer salvageable, so it will either end up as some sort of yard art or in the crusher. It's a sad fate for a classic that wasn't terrible after decades off the road, but at least we can see it getting smashed on the track toward the end of the video. The demolition derby footage starts at the 23-minute mark.

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Car Nuts Got One-Owner '68 Chevy C10 Survivor, Cut It Into 1,200-HP Slammed, Blown SEMA Monstrosity
73 photos
Photo: YouTube/Autotopia LA
Chevrolet’s pickup trucks have long been a staple of hot rodding, custom-building culture, because… well, because why not? With pickups assembled in such abundant numbers, and with a far lesser following that mainstream classics from the fifties, sixties, seventies, and eighties, pickups are the go-to choice for builders who want to go completely nuts without Frankensteining a legend into a wild one-off.
Some custom trucks politely nod to classic heritage. This one straps a towering supercharger to a 427-cubic-inch V8 and declares war on rear tires, climate change, and the owner’s budget – all in one blow. In the recent years, we’ve grown more and more accustomed to 1,000+ hp pickup trucks (thanks a lot, Hennessey!), but those are all NEW trucks.
This old Chevy, on the other hand, looks like it’ll molt its sheet metal in flakes at the slightest touch of the loud pedal. Fear not, it’s just an optical illusion. Just like its stance , which could embody the sixty-two-year fresh Pontiac GTO tag line "If it clung to the road any closer, it'd be a white line." When's the last time you saw a white line begin where two black ones end?
Right after SEMA 2026 wrapped up in Las Vegas, Autotopia LA host Shawn Davis met Mikey Rolleri and Andrew Riviera of Salvage to Savage. Fresh off the Toyo Tires Treadpass display, their slammed 1968 Chevrolet C10 looks like a colossal engine wearing vintage sheetmetal.
Photo: YouTube/Autotopia LA Before the South Florida crew got their hands on it, this stepside pickup was an untouched, one-owner survivor in southern Georgia. Andrew and Mikey hauled it out of a barn at 1:00 AM in 40-degree weather, becoming its second owners before immediately cutting it up. Purists flooded their YouTube channel with hate for modifying a clean survivor, yet the builders stayed unfazed, insisting they transformed a sleepy farm truck into something better.
Factory ledgers explain that purist debate while validating Andrew's point about sheer production volume. Chevrolet built 609,465 commercial vehicles in 1968 , including approximately 355,000 half-ton C10 models.
Smooth Fleetside pickups dominated output with 294,000 units, whereas fendered Stepside pickups accounted for 45,000 examples, including roughly 34,000 short-bed trucks. Another 12,000 Suburbans, 4,000 bare Chassis-Cab units, and 3,500 enclosed Panel trucks completed the series, leaving plenty of steel for wild builds.
Photo: YouTube/Autotopia LA Their central design goal was gloriously unhinged: build a dedicated burnout machine with an induction stack reaching the roofline. Under the open hood sits a forged 427-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) V8 motorsports crate engine from BluePrint Engines, packed with a forged crankshaft, forged pistons, and LS7-style aluminum cylinder heads.
A Holley Low-Ram intake supports a Tick Performance air-to-water intercooler and a tall billet spacer built strictly to elevate the hardware above the fenders. Crowning that skyscraper of billet aluminum is a 3.0-liter Magnuson M.O.A.B. supercharger topped by dual Holley EFI throttle bodies and four CNC-machined velocity stacks.
Eric at Origin Wheels cut those intake trumpets to match his custom wheels, while Holley electronic fuel injection and a Dominator ECU manage fueling. Alongside the block, symmetrical, near-equal-length stainless headers fabricated by Arton from Nitrodyne snake into fender-exit dumps that growl like a Top Fuel dragster.
Photo: YouTube/Autotopia LA While the complete combination is built to support 1,200 horsepower, the intense 10-month SEMA crunch left zero time for a full dyno session. Because the current pulley ratio does not spin the 3.0-liter blower fast enough to create positive boost, the forged 427 runs naturally aspirated. Even unboosted, the big-inch V8 churns out 620 crank horsepower, safeguarded by a dry-sump oiling system with a large bay-mounted reservoir tank.
Behind the engine sits a bulletproof driveline tailored specifically for high-speed tire torture. Power flows through an FTI-built Turbo 400 three-speed automatic transmission controlled by a drag-style reverse manual shifter, then down a 4-inch steel two-piece driveshaft from Knoxville Driveline. Out back, a Quick Performance Ford 9-inch rear end houses 35-spline chromoly axles and tall 3.40 gears, allowing the rear tires to approach 200 mph of wheel speed during smoke shows.
Underneath the oxidized white patina bodywork lies a custom RevB perimeter chassis built by Scott Nelson in Arizona, featuring open frame windows for hidden wiring and integrated height-sensor mounts. An AccuAir suspension drops the C10 onto its rockers over Origin Wheels bronze rims measuring 20x8.5 inches front and 20x10 inches rear. Wrapped in 245/40 and 295/35 Toyo tires, the narrow rear setup clears the stepside fenders while Wilwood brakes handle stopping.
Photo: YouTube/Autotopia LA Mikey Rolleri showcased his metalworking chops by fabricating the aluminum inner fenders and a heavy 14-gauge steel tailgate spoiler emblazoned with RevB lettering. Inside the bed sits a handmade aluminum intercooler reservoir fed by a 30-gallon-per-minute Davies Craig pump with an internal anti-aeration return tube. A Radium Engineering fuel cell pairs one lift pump with two staged Hellcat pumps, while cut-down Peterbilt semi mirrors and a cab-side kill switch complete the exterior.
Inside the cab, race-bred functionality blends with unexpected bespoke style. Mikey welded a bronze-finished roll cage with lowered door bars and generous headroom so Shawn Davis could climb in effortlessly without bumping his skull. Brushed aluminum door panels wear geometric black-and-gold fabric borrowed from Greasy Hands Society jacket liners, matching the bucket seats. Joes Racing sprint-car pedals, a Rad Industries hydraulic handbrake, and a Holley digital dash command the cockpit.
Once Mikey strapped in and fired the 427, the cabin filled with raw mechanical thunder. A blown power steering line from cruising the Las Vegas Arts District the previous night meant heavy manual steering, while the towering blower and velocity stacks obscured forward visibility on right turns. This isn’t meant to turn corners anyway, so why bother with annoying details?
Photo: YouTube/Autotopia LA Despite the deafening exhaust note and missing power assist, Shawn marveled at how planted, composed, and surprisingly safe the slammed pickup felt on public roads. Back in the Rev City lot, Mikey hit a console switch activating a Wilwood rear brake solenoid that isolates hydraulic pressure to the rear calipers, alongside a trans-brake button.
With only the front wheels clamped down, he pinned the throttle and unleashed a ferocious burnout that swallowed the entire building in thick white smoke. Fresh rubber caked beneath the rear bumper already hinted at a 15-second rev-limiter session the night before.
When the smoke finally cleared, twin black stripes stretched across the asphalt as proof of concept. Exhausted from a full week at SEMA 2026, Shawn admitted he was grateful the 3.0-liter Magnuson blower was only along for the ride, keeping output at a friendly 620 horsepower rather than the full 1,200-horsepower fury to come. Even at half strength, this Salvage to Savage creation stands as one of the wildest C10 builds ever.

New Gran Turismo 7 Time Trial Is Here and I Can Drive My Favorite Car in the World Again
27 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I think 95% of my friends are as obsessed with cars as I am. We talk so much about the topic that normal people can’t really stand being around for more than a few hours. Well, we can obviously stick to other aspects of life, but then we are the ones who get bored of the conversation.
It’s often funny how easily we can connect to new like-minded people just through our common love of cars. I recently made a new friend, and he also owns an FC RX-7. He loves drifting and Initial D just as much as I do, and it was hilarious to me to find out that he’s just as picky with food as I am.
You could say we’re built on the same pattern, which is why it was so easy for us to get along. We even agreed to play CS:GO and Assetto Corsa when he gets back home. And I should probably invite for a few laps in Gran Turismo 7 , too.
Speaking of which, it’s easy to see signs everywhere you look if you’ve only got one thing on your mind. The newest Time Trial in the game features a 1991 Mazda RX-7 Type R (FD), and we get to drive it around Watkins Glen International Long Course.
The only downside is that someone at Polyphony decided the car would be rolling on Comfort Soft tires, which is something many people have already been complaining about online. Oh well, let me show you what I did for practice.
Practice Session 1 Photo: autoevolution I sent this new friend of mine to visit my buddy Mike, where my RX-7 is currently waiting for an engine rebuild. My friend Omar was also there, and he shot a 10 minute long video of the FC as Nikos wanted to hear it run, sit inside and so on so forth.
I almost never have the patience or time to sit through a 10-minute long video in the middle of the day, but this time I almost had tears in my eyes doing so. Two years have gone by since I last drove it, and the only way to soothe the pain is to get back behind the wheel of one in Gran Turismo 7.
I even opted for the Furinkazan look, as that’s my favorite non-drifting version of the car. Seeing as the Time Trial FD is bone stock, I knew using 450 hp on the FC for practice wouldn’t be smart. I switched back to a stock turbo and ECU, reducing the engine output to 259 bhp while retaining all the chassis upgrades.
Because of the tires, both understeer and oversteer occurred throughout the lap but keeping the car in check wasn’t difficult. My best lap was a 2:10.447 after two attempts and the only thing I could think of was: When are we getting an IMSA GTO replica or at least an NA FC in the game?
Practice Session 2 Photo: autoevolution You see, this time I didn’t ask about the first-gen RX-7, even I’ve been thinking about it for a few years now. We didn’t need three variations of the FD in the game, especially since you can customize your car the way you want it from both a visual and mechanical perspective.
I used my version of the Time Trial car for the second practice session, albeit giving up on the 488 bhp setup in favor of a more tame 327 bhp engine.
I didn’t have any weight reduction packages this time, but was still faster down the main straight compared to the FC. With the extra power it felt more fun and more playful, but it was obviously not as nimble through the corners.
As a result, my lap time was half a second slower, but there’s no denying that this thing looks like poetry in motion (especially with the Red Suns design).
Practice Session 3 Photo: autoevolution I moved on to the 2002 Spirit R version of the FD for the next session, and this one has the dark green finish and yellow wheels I enjoy so much.
With all the upgrades, power levels were up at 586 bhp while the overall weight is only 2,240 lbs/1,016 kg. Even after trying to make it slower, it still has 378 bhp and I was about to discover the car also had a racing gearbox to move around.
While the previous two RX-7s felt a bit too slow for my taste, this version of the FD was the perfect mix for the job at hand. I found myself hitting 156 mph/251 kph down the main straight, and it didn’t take long to discover I was way too confident with the brakes.
I quickly adapted my strategy for the next lap, and got it down to 2:04.825: that’s something you won’t be able to extract from the standard FD at Watkins Glen.
Practice Session 4 Photo: autoevolution Gran Turismo 7 even has an RE Amemiya version of the FD RX-7 in the game, which is great. I’m sure Liberty Walk and Pandem have won the hearts of many with their take on Mazda’s iconic machine, but I will forever be a loyal follower of what Ama-san has done with these cars.
I just need to find $70K or so to build my dream FD, and it might just look like the one I have in the game if I ever get there.
This one uses the stock transmission and has 395 bhp after the changes I’ve made. It was considerably slower than the Spirit R down the main straight, but on par with the other RX-7s here.
I was shocked to see my best lap was only 0.003 seconds faster than the one I recorded in the FC. It gives me hope that I’ll still be able to pull of some good result in my real-world car.
New Time Trial Photo: autoevolution So, Watkins Glen Long Course is back on the menu. Can you even remember the last time it was part of the Time Trial? You need to go back to January of this year, when the fastest driver in the world needed just a little two minutes for a complete lap of it in the Lexus LC500 .
While that car is quite a bit heavier, it also has more power, an automatic gearbox on top of the SH tires available for the event. Meanwhile, user holl01 is currently on top of the Global Rankings with a 2:08.786, and he is just one of two drivers to have dipped bellow the 2:09 marker so far!
The target for the Gold Record Reward is quite a bit more relaxed by comparison, sitting at 2:12.649. If you’re exactly nine seconds slower, you still have a small chance to get the Bronze Record Reward. I looked at Tidgney’s tutorial for the lap after I was done with mine, and I’m slightly shocked to see him using fourth gear for the chicane.
I should try it next. I used a Montego Blue version of the bone stock FD but forgot to take pictures of it, so another shot of Keisuke’s Touge Monster will have to do for now. I scored a 2:17.218 after two laps, and was eager to increase the pace a bit for my last stint of the day.
Sugo Personal Best Attempt Photo: autoevolution Since I paid 20 million credits for the McLaren F1 GTR, I plan to drive it around every single track in the game. My laps at the Nordschleife were the most exciting ones so far, and Sugo was next on the menu. I haven’t racked up enough miles here since it arrived with Part One of Spec IV.
I removed the turbocharger that I used at Le Mans, and the car still felt like a teleportation device. I was up at 167 mph/270 kph before Turn One, and only needed 81 seconds for the complete lap. I was just barely faster in the supercharged version of the Mercedes-Benz CLK-LM '98 as it struggled with the technical corners at Sugo.
Moving on to the F3500-A was like engaging warp speed, and I went through three failed laps before stopping the clock at 1:09.129. Still, the ultimate “I want to be scared to death” experience comes by driving the almost ancient F1500-T.
I wasn’t brave or skilled enough to extract its maximum potential, which is why I was ultimately one second slower in it than I was in the naturally-aspirated F3500-A. I’ll be back with my take on the latest Weekly Challenges tomorrow!

"Unsinkable" Bayesian Superyacht Sank Because of Crew Incompetence, Not Design Flaw
10 photos
Photo: Perini Navi
How does a luxury sailing yacht designed to be unsinkable even in adverse weather sink in less than 30 minutes, during a freak storm, while anchored in shallow water? If that yacht is the Bayesian, which did just that in August 2024, the answer is "crew negligence."
The preliminary report from the Termini Imerese Prosecutor's Office, which has been investigating the tragedy , points the finger at the crew of the Bayesian and not some suspected design flaw. Three crew members, including the captain, are under investigation for the incident that claimed the lives of seven people on August 19, 2024, just off the port of Porticello, Italy.
While a previous report by the UK's Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) noted that a design flaw of the Bayesian was largely responsible for the sinking, the Prosecutor's Office says it as the crew's experience, and ultimately negligence, that's to blame. The full report has not yet been submitted, but a synopsis has been provided to the local media .
According to the findings, the crew should have had the keel of the Bayesian fully extended, allowing it to bounce back after listing. Warnings for bad weather on that night had been sent out in advance, so the sudden gusts of wind that broke out at past 3 o'clock in the morning should not have taken the crew by surprise, finding them unprepared.
Photo: Perini Navi/ Danny Wheelz Because the keel wasn't fully extended, when one gust of wind hit the Bayesian sideways at speeds of 70 knots (80.5 mph/129.5 kph), the vessel listed and wasn't capable of returning to an even keel. Instead, it began to take on water and, in just 27 minutes, it had sunk completely.
Prior to the findings , reports claimed that a design flaw must have caused the incident, specifically its record-setting mast. Bayesian was a luxury sailing yacht built by Perini Navi in 2008, equipped with the tallest aluminum mast in the world. That 75-meter (246-foot) mast was believed to have dragged the ship down when it listed, working against its in-built ability to bounce back to an even keel.
The Bayesian was raised from the seabed in June 2025, but only after the mast was separated from the vessel. In the spring of 2026, The Italian Sea Group (TISG), which owns the Perini Navi brand, Admiral, and Tecnomar, announced it would be filing for bankruptcy, with an auction for all brands scheduled to take place later this month.
Photo: Perini Navi Bayesian was owned by British billionaire Mike Lynch, who died in the incident together with his 18-year-old daughter. The ship was launched in 2008 as Salute and, because of its characteristics and that record-setting mast, soon became a legend. Perini Navi themselves described it more than once as "unsinkable."
